statement: For every one of the 13^6 labelled weak-order preference profiles on the unweighted complete bipartite graph K_{3,3}, with every acceptable partner strictly preferred to being unmatched and with all 34 partial matchings admitted as alternatives, there is a popular-winning singleton or a popular-winning unordered pair of distinct matchings. Moreover, the profile ((0,0,0),(0,1,2),(0,2,1),(0,2,1),(1,2,0),(1,0,0)) has no popular-winning singleton. Therefore the maximum popular dimension over the frozen domain is exactly 2.
contribution: This exactly resolves the frozen finite K_{3,3} census. An order-72 orbit enumeration, Burnside fixed-point check, and separately implemented unreduced enumeration agree that 4,826,131 labelled profiles have dimension 1 and 678 have dimension 2, with none of dimension 3. A pure-Python certificate verifies the explicit lower-bound profile and a winning pair. No priority claim beyond resolving the frozen question is asserted.
